title: Allan Gray Scholarship Programme 2026: Fully Supported High School Scholarship for Young South African Entrepreneurs
summary: The Allan Gray Scholarship Programme for Entrepreneurial Development 2026 is an opportunity for academically capable, financially deserving Grade 6 learners in South Africa who demonstrate curiosity, entrepreneurial potential and a desire to create value in their communities. Offered by the Allan Gray Orbis Foundation , the programme goes beyond conventional financial assistance. Successful scholars receive support to attend leading partner high schools while also gaining access to mentorship, entrepreneurial development, leadership opportunities, workshops, online learning and a community of like-minded young people. The programme is designed to identify promising young learners at an early stage and give them the educational environment, resources and developmental support needed to grow their academic abilities and entrepreneurial potential. The Foundation s current information confirms that the 2026 application deadline is 15 September 2026 . Applications posted after 15 September 2026 will not be considered. Opportunity Overview Opportunity: Allan Gray Scholarship Programme for Entrepreneurial Development Category: High School Scholarship Provider: Allan Gray Orbis Foundation Target group: Current Grade 6 learners Country: South Africa Citizenship requirement: South African citizenship Age requirement: Applicants must be 11 or 12 years old in Grade 6 Eligible birth years: 2014 or 2015 Academic requirement: Minimum 70% in English and Mathematics Financial requirement: Applicants must demonstrate financial need Application status: Applications are currently open Application deadline: 15 September 2026 Programme focus: Education, entrepreneurship, leadership and personal development Application methods: Online application and application form, subject to the Foundation s submission requirements About the Allan Gray Scholarship Programme The Allan Gray Scholarship Programme is designed for young learners who demonstrate more than academic ability. The Foundation seeks learners with a curious and entrepreneurial mindset , the potential to excel academically and a genuine financial need. Rather than treating a scholarship simply as a means of paying school fees, the programme takes a long-term approach to developing young people. Scholars are introduced to entrepreneurial thinking, leadership, collaboration, problem-solving and value creation while continuing their formal high school education. The programme is part of the Allan Gray Orbis Foundation s broader commitment to identifying and developing entrepreneurial potential in Southern Africa. The Foundation describes entrepreneurship as an important avenue for creating meaningful employment and contributing to social and economic transformation. What Makes This Scholarship Different? Many scholarships focus primarily on academic funding. The Allan Gray Scholarship Programme takes a more holistic approach. Successful scholars can receive financial assistance for their schooling while simultaneously participating in developmental interventions intended to strengthen their confidence, leadership abilities, entrepreneurial thinking and personal growth. The Foundation s model combines: Academic support Financial assistance Entrepreneurial development Mentorship Leadership development Peer learning Online learning Workshops and seminars Community engagement Exposure to entrepreneurship and value creation This approach means that scholars are not simply supported through high school; they are introduced to a developmental environment intended to prepare them for future opportunities. Who Can Apply? The scholarship is specifically designed for young learners currently in Grade 6 . Applicants must meet the Foundation s eligibility conditions before submitting an application. 1. Current Grade 6 Learner The applicant must be a current Grade 6 learner in 2026 . This is an important requirement because the scholarship is intended to support learners transitioning from primary school into high school. 2. South African Citizenship The applicant must be a South African citizen . This means the programme is not a general international scholarship and is not open to applicants from other African countries or other continents. 3. Age Requirement Applicants must be: At least 11 years old; and Not older than 12 years old in Grade 6. For the 2026 application cycle, eligible applicants should have been born in 2014 or 2015 . 4. Academic Performance Applicants must obtain a minimum of: 70% in English 70% in Mathematics The academic requirement is intended to identify learners who have demonstrated the potential to succeed in a demanding high-school environment. 5. Financial Need Applicants must demonstrate that they are financially deserving . Financial need is an important part of the selection process because the programme is intended to provide educational opportunities to learners who may otherwise face financial barriers to accessing leading high schools. Applicants and their parents or legal guardians should therefore pay close attention to the financial documentation requested as part of the application. Entrepreneurial Potential Is Important The Allan Gray Scholarship is not simply a traditional academic scholarship. The Foundation is looking for young people who demonstrate qualities associated with an entrepreneurial mindset. These may include: Curiosity Initiative Problem-solving ability Leadership potential Desire to create value Positive attitude Growth mindset Willingness to collaborate Interest in entrepreneurship Ability to think creatively Confidence and willingness to learn A learner does not necessarily have to already own a business to demonstrate entrepreneurial potential. The programme is intended to cultivate and develop entrepreneurial thinking , allowing young people to understand how they can identify problems, develop ideas, create value and contribute positively to society. What Does the Allan Gray Scholarship Cover? One of the strongest aspects of the opportunity is the breadth of support available to successful scholars. 1. Tuition and Boarding The scholarship provides support for tuition and boarding , helping successful learners attend participating leading high schools without carrying the normal financial burden associated with these expenses. 2. Monthly Allowance Scholars receive a monthly allowance , providing additional financial support during their studies. 3. Toiletries and Clothing The scholarship also provides support for essential personal items, including: Toiletries School uniforms Casual clothing 4. Extra-Mural Activities Support is provided for extra-mural activities , enabling scholars to participate in activities outside the traditional classroom environment. This can contribute to personal development, teamwork, confidence and leadership. 5. Stationery and Textbooks The scholarship covers educational materials such as: Stationery Textbooks This ensures that scholars have important resources needed for their academic work. Entrepreneurial and Personal Development Benefits Financial assistance is only one component of the programme. The Foundation also provides a range of developmental opportunities designed to help scholars become confident and entrepreneurial young people. Workshops Scholars participate in workshops that expose them to concepts and experiences beyond their normal school curriculum. Annual Entrepreneurial Conference Participants have access to an annual entrepreneurial conference , providing exposure to entrepreneurial ideas, speakers, learning experiences and other participants. Online Learning Campus Scholars receive access to an Online Learning Campus , allowing them to participate in digital learning and development opportunities. Programme Officer Mentorship Each scholar can benefit from guidance and mentorship from a dedicated Programme Officer . Mentorship is intended to help learners navigate their personal and developmental journey while encouraging them to explore their potential. Like-Minded Community Scholars become part of a community of young people who share an interest in learning, leadership, entrepreneurship and personal development. This environment can encourage collaboration, peer learning and long-term relationships. Skills and Qualities Scholars Can Develop Through the combination of financial support, education and entrepreneurial development, the programme aims to help participants develop several important qualities. Confidence Young people are encouraged to develop greater confidence in their abilities, ideas and potential. Entrepreneurial Mindset Scholars learn to think differently about challenges, opportunities and value creation. Growth Mindset The programme encourages learners to view learning and development as an ongoing process. Leadership Participants are exposed to experiences designed to strengthen leadership qualities and their ability to positively influence others. Problem-Solving Entrepreneurial development encourages learners to identify challenges and think about possible solutions. Collaboration The programme places emphasis on community and collaboration, helping scholars understand the importance of working with others. Mentorship and Development Mentorship is an important part of the Allan Gray approach. The Foundation combines face-to-face learning, online learning, peer learning and individual interventions to nurture the potential already demonstrated by participating learners. Rather than expecting a young person to develop independently, the programme provides structured support throughout the scholar s journey. This can help learners develop a stronger understanding of entrepreneurship while also building confidence and leadership skills. How the Application and Selection Process Works Applicants should understand that submitting an application does not automatically guarantee a scholarship. The selection process involves several stages. Step 1: Submit the Application Applicants must submit the required application form together with the necessary supporting documentation. The Foundation provides an online application option as well as an official application form. Applicants should ensure that all required sections are completed correctly and that the requested supporting documents are included. Step 2: Foundation Assessment Successful applicants will be required to write a Foundation assessment in English and Mathematics at Grade 6 level in December 2026 . This assessment forms part of the selection process. Step 3: Interviews After the Foundation assessment, successful candidates will be invited to interviews in early 2027 . The interviews provide an opportunity for the selection team to learn more about candidates beyond their academic results. Step 4: Placement School Interviews Recommended candidates will subsequently be invited to participating placement schools for interviews. This means that selection involves both the Foundation and the relevant school. Step 5: Scholarship Award Candidates whose recommendations are approved by the placement schools will be awarded the Allan Gray Scholarship. According to the programme information, scholarship awards are expected in May 2027 . Step 6: Memorandum of Agreement Once the scholarship has been awarded, the Foundation, placement school and the scholar s custodian will sign a Memorandum of Agreement . This formalises the scholarship arrangement and the responsibilities of the relevant parties. Important Documents and Application Requirements Applicants should carefully review the official application form before submitting their application. The 2026 application documentation states that applicants must provide supporting academic documentation, including certified copies of the applicant s Grade 5 fourth-term report and Grade 6 second-term report . The reports must show the applicant s name, grade and school. Failure to provide the required documentation can result in automatic disqualification. Parents or legal guardians should also provide an active cellphone number and valid email address because these may be used for communication concerning the application. title: Wilson Center Congressional Fellowship Program 2026: Six-Week Foreign Policy Fellowship for Congressional Staff
summary: The Wilson Center Congressional Fellowship Program (CFP) is a six-week professional development fellowship designed for current Congressional staff who want to deepen their understanding of global affairs, debate major foreign policy issues, and connect with leading experts and policymakers. The programme brings together Congressional staffers from across the political aisle and creates an environment where participants can exchange ideas, examine complex international issues, and develop stronger professional networks. About the Congressional Fellowship Program The Wilson Center s Congressional Fellowship Program focuses on foreign policy, global affairs and the legislative process . Throughout the six-week seminar, Fellows engage with leading foreign policy thinkers and practitioners. Sessions are designed to encourage analytical thinking, fresh perspectives and informed debate around important international issues. The programme also includes an interactive simulation intended to encourage Fellows from across the political aisle to network, collaborate and work together . What Does the Fellowship Offer? Selected Fellows will participate in a structured six-week seminar covering key global and foreign policy issues. The programme provides opportunities to: Debate major international and foreign policy issues. Engage with leading foreign policy experts and practitioners. Develop analytical approaches to complex global issues. Gain fresh perspectives through discussions and recommended readings. Network with Congressional staff from across the political aisle. Participate in an interactive simulation. Connect with policymakers, academics and executives through the Wilson Center community. Certificate of Completion Fellows are expected to attend the majority of the programme sessions. Participants who attend at least five of the six sessions will receive a certificate of completion from the Wilson Center . Successful Fellows will also become part of the Woodrow Wilson Congressional Fellowship Alumni Network . Access to the Wilson Center Alumni Network One of the long-term benefits of the programme is continued access to the Wilson Center s alumni community. The programme has an alumni network of approximately 1,000 members , providing Fellows with opportunities to maintain professional connections after completing the programme. Alumni may also be invited to participate in exclusive Wilson Center opportunities, including: Private briefings Study trips around the world High-level roundtables Other Wilson Center events and activities Alumni can also draw upon the expertise of Wilson Center experts, including policymakers, academics and executives from both the public and private sectors. Who Is the Fellowship For? The Congressional Fellowship Program is specifically designed for mid- to senior-level Congressional staff . Applicants should: Be current Congressional staff . Have a strong understanding of the legislative process. Have an interest in foreign policy. Aspire to pursue or continue a career focused on shaping foreign policy. Be able to attend at least five of the six required sessions. The programme is therefore not presented as a general fellowship open to students, recent graduates or members of the general public.
